title: Gap analysis interviews
source_system: Interviews (all 7 staff and the MSP lead technician)

Owner (2026-07-21): cyber risk was considered only at insurance renewal and security outcomes are not reviewed. Owner and Operations Manager (2026-07-21): they did not know the Florida 30-day notice clocks, the 10-day duty of third-party agents or the E-Verify MOU's immediate notice to DHS; there is no incident response or contingency plan. Operations Manager (2026-07-22): no vendor SOC 2 report has been requested, no threat information is received, security performance is not measured, and the Form I-9 scans and paper files are not checked. Coordinator (2026-07-22): bank-change requests by phone, email or text are not tied to a verified identity; she did not know the payroll vendor can freeze bank changes and recall deposits; there is no written scanning process or E-Verify outage procedure, and no outage has occurred; the remote alternative procedure is not used. Staff (2026-07-22): a suspected incident would be told to a colleague; nobody watches payroll bank changes, exports or E-Verify user activity; recruiters text candidates from personal phones and receive ID photos there. Account Manager (2026-07-23): client security expectations arrive as questionnaires and contract clauses that are not tracked, and security evidence could help win larger warehouse clients. Senior Recruiter (2026-07-23): the AI feature and filter were turned on without anyone else knowing; payroll notification settings were changed in 2025 with no record. MSP lead technician (2026-07-24): no single sign-on or federation is used, the firm develops no software, office bandwidth serves 7 users, and no backup restore has ever been run
